newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's main union leader sits high school exams.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's main union leader sits high school exams.

text.p: The leader of Brazil's largest union, a veteran of talks with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, beamed on Tuesday after passing the first hurdle to gaining his secondary school diploma, Globo television said.

Vicente Paulo da Silva, better known as Vicentinho, passed four out of the eight required exams for the high school degree after completing a correspondence course co-sponsored by the Sao Paulo State Industries Federation (Fiesp).
Vicentinho, leader of the Single Workers' Confederation, is no stranger to the corridors of power in Brasilia but his formal education only stretches until the end of primary school.

The popular union leader, whose trademark lisp is familiar to millions of television viewers, aims to become a lawyer. He is due to stand down as CUT leader later this year and is rumoured to be considering running for election in Congress.
"I want to be a lawyer to defend workers, including against Fiesp itself," he said.
